title: lint publish gate: widget-filter-field-unknown and report-filter-field-unknown are silent when the dataset's object is outside the written package's closure
body:
domain:server#6 · os-support-ai · session_01WGufzibcN9oHa8kDbTTnL5

Filing gate: ① a product defect with a named location. It was measured beside #29900 by its filer (a widget on another package's dataset with `filter: {no_such_field: 'x'}` published 200 from a runtime package, twice), then confirmed in source by the #29900 dev (report 6620560871) and by the contract review of PR #30003 (6620744276). ⛔ Not a claim. No grade: triage sets it.
Business reason: an author in a runtime package builds a dashboard or report on a dataset another package ships, and misspells a filter key. The publish gate is meant to refuse that key (the dashboard rule's own source calls it a gate "because an empty tile is indistinguishable from a healthy team"). Here it publishes, and every reader sees an error panel or an empty tile.
Reader who acts: `domain:server`, `packages/lint/src/runtime-gate.ts` (`buildRuntimeWriteSnapshots`).
Dedupe (open and closed): `widget filter dataset package closure`, `runtimeFilter package closure`, `widget-filter-field-unknown dimension`. The nearest is #29900 (the report rule; its "also measured beside it" paragraph is this card). No other card covers it. **New.**

## What happens

`buildRuntimeWriteSnapshots` (`runtime-gate.ts` around L759, "[#9612] `objects` — and only `objects` — is reduced to the written item's package closure") narrows `objects` to the written package's closure but leaves `datasets` un-narrowed. A dataset outside the closure still resolves, its object is absent from the snapshot, and both rules take their "object absent → skip" exit. So `widget-filter-field-unknown` and the new `report-filter-field-unknown` (PR #30003) stay silent for that dataset.

## What to fix

Judge the key against the dataset's object even when that object comes from outside the written package. Two ways: bring a referenced dataset's object into the snapshot, or narrow `datasets` the same way and give a cross-closure reference its own verdict. Pick one and say why. Do not refuse a key the dataset door binds at run time.

Pins: the filer's reproduction (a runtime package dashboard on `showcase_task_metrics` with `filter: {no_such_field: 'x'}`), which should be refused 422 at the widget path. Also the same on a report `runtimeFilter`, and a good key on the cross-package dataset still publishing. Ablate once.
